review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–121). It has no @[simp] attributes, no simp-set definitions, and no equalities that could serve as rewrite rules or cycle. Its declarations are one cardinal inequality, three finiteness statements (two of them theorems and one an instance), a Nat.card ≤ finrank inequality in two forms, and a set-finiteness statement. All of them are inequalities or finiteness facts with side hypotheses (such as the rank bound `Module.rank R C < ℵ₀`) or typeclass assumptions. None is a rewrite identity, so none is a sound simp-lemma candidate. Finiteness is already exposed through the `instFinite` instance, so the usual `Finite`-instance route covers it. Adding simp attributes to the inequalities would not give a canonical normal form. I did not search downstream uses for a missing simp rule. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
